subtitle: On the Monsoon Shore, a Pepper War Topples an Empire’s Pride

panels.shot: wide, stormy shoreline tableau with opposing figures facing each other across a wind‑lashed bay
panels.action: Marthanda Varma stands firm on a rain‑dark Colachel shore facing Eustachius De Lannoy in Dutch armour, Dutch ships looming offshore and Travancore troops massed behind, waves crashing between them under heavy monsoon clouds.

dialogue.text: In 1741 at Colachel, a rising pepper kingdom shattered Dutch power, and from a defeated captain forged the steel of Travancore.

i18n.hi: 1741, कोलाचेल में, उभरते मिर्च राज्य ने डच ताकत तोड़ी, और हारे कप्तान से त्रावणकोर की इस्पाती ढाल गढ़ी।

panels.shot: slow panoramic sweep along the Malabar coast, following merchant ships
panels.action: A line of European and Indian sailing ships rides the Arabian Sea along the Malabar coast, with lush green hills inland and small port towns clinging to the shore under a hazy tropical sky.

dialogue.text: Along the Malabar coast, pepper was not just spice; it was gold on the sea, and the Dutch Company staked its fortune on it.

i18n.hi: मालाबार तट पर काली मिर्च मसाला नहीं, समंदर का सोना थी, और डच कंपनी ने उस पर अपनी किस्मत दांव पर लगा दी थी।

panels.shot: medium wide of a Dutch factory compound at a coastal port
panels.action: Inside a sturdy Dutch trading compound with tiled roofs and a flagpole, European factors bargain with local chiefs and brokers over sacks of pepper piled in a courtyard, clerks bent over ledgers.

dialogue.text: By the 1730s the VOC held forts, factories and pepper contracts, guarding allied chiefs on the coast as much as its own ledgers.

i18n.hi: 1730 के दशक तक VOC के किले, कोठियां और मिर्च के ठेके थे, जो तटीय सरदारों और अपनी खाता‑किताब दोनों की रखवाली करते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on a younger Marthanda Varma in court, with map spread
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, in regal attire, stands over a palm‑leaf map of southern Kerala laid on a low table, courtiers around him as he gestures decisively toward a patchwork of small chiefdoms between the Western Ghats and the sea.

dialogue.text: To their south, Marthanda Varma of Travancore saw a broken land of petty chiefs and vowed to weld it into a single shielded kingdom.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में त्रावणकोर के मार्तांडा वर्मा ने बिखरी रियासतों को देखा और कसम खाई कि इन्हें एक ढाल बने राज्य में गढ़ेंगे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over a campaign map transitioning to marching columns
panels.action: The map of southern Malabar blurs into real terrain as Travancore infantry and Nair warriors march through coconut groves, small hill forts in the distance lowering their flags as emissaries ride between them and Marthanda Varma’s camp.

dialogue.text: Through diplomacy, war and annexation, he moved north, absorbing chiefdom after chiefdom, closing his hand around the pepper hills.

i18n.hi: संधि, युद्ध और विलय से वो उत्तर बढ़े, रियासत दर रियासत समेटते हुए, मिर्च पहाड़ियों पर अपनी पकड़ कसते गए।

panels.shot: interior of a Dutch council chamber in Cochin, candlelit
panels.action: In a wood‑panelled Dutch council room, Eustachius De Lannoy stands among other officers and officials as a senior VOC councillor angrily points at a map where Travancore territory presses against Dutch‑allied pepper regions.

dialogue.text: The Dutch saw contracts slipping away, allies overrun, and profits fall. To them, Travancore was no pious kingdom, but a dangerous commercial rival.

i18n.hi: डचों ने ठेके हाथ से निकलते, साथी कुचले जाते और मुनाफे गिरते देखे। उनके लिए त्रावणकोर भक्त राज्य नहीं, खतरनाक कारोबारी दुश्मन था।

panels.shot: close on a Dutch letter and then Marthanda Varma reading in his court
panels.action: A Dutch ultimatum stamped with the VOC seal lies open, its script neat and severe; in the next moment Marthanda Varma sits in his audience hall, calmly reading the same letter while a courtier waits tensely.

dialogue.text: From Batavia, Governor-General van Imhoff sent sharp words: halt your advance, respect our pepper rights, obey our treaties.

i18n.hi: बाटाविया से गवर्नर‑जनरल वान इमहोफ ने कड़ा पैगाम भेजा: बढ़त रोको, हमारे मिर्च अधिकार मानो, संधियाँ निभाओ।

panels.shot: medium on Marthanda Varma handing back the letter with a composed face
panels.action: Marthanda Varma, seated on a low throne, returns the Dutch letter to his envoy with a faint, unreadable smile, behind him a mural showing the goddess protecting Travancore’s hills and sea.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma_and_eustachius_de_lannoy
dialogue.text: Tell them: my land is not for sale with their pepper.

i18n.hi: उन्हें कह दो: मेरी जमीन उनके मिर्च के साथ बिकाऊ नहीं।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle of Dutch ships in rough monsoon seas nearing the coast
panels.action: Under a brooding monsoon sky, Dutch warships and transports ride heavy swells as they close in on the Travancore coast, sailors straining at ropes while Eustachius De Lannoy watches from the quarterdeck in armour.

dialogue.text: In 1739 the pepper quarrel turned to war. Dutch fleets and muskets would, they thought, teach this inland king his limits.

i18n.hi: 1739 में मिर्च की नोकझोंक युद्ध बन गई। डच जहाज़ और बंदूकें सोचती थीं कि इस पहाड़ी राजा को उसकी हद दिखा देंगी।

panels.shot: montage-like wide showing Dutch advances along the coast
panels.action: A composite scene shows Dutch detachments marching through coastal villages, seizing small forts, and raising the VOC flag over a captured outpost while local chiefs look on anxiously from a distance.

dialogue.text: At first they moved quickly, taking coastal posts, backing Travancore’s foes, hoping to squeeze the kingdom away from the sea.

i18n.hi: शुरू में वे फुर्ती से बढ़े, तटीय चौकियां घेर लीं, त्रावणकोर के दुश्मनों को सहारा दिया, ताकि राज्य को समंदर से काट दें।

panels.shot: interior of a Dutch office in Batavia, cluttered and strained
panels.action: In Batavia’s VOC headquarters, harried officials pore over crowded ledgers and dispatches, a globe and charts of the East Indies behind them, while a clerk points to mounting debts and scattered red‑ink notes.

dialogue.text: But the Company was stretched. Batavia’s wars, debts and distant garrisons thinned the reinforcements that Malabar cried for.

i18n.hi: पर कंपनी खुद खिंच चुकी थी। बाटाविया के युद्ध, कर्ज और दूर के छावनियों ने मलाबार के लिए आने वाली मदद पतली कर दी।

panels.shot: medium wide in Travancore camp with Marthanda Varma addressing commanders
panels.action: In a rain‑damp field camp, Marthanda Varma stands beneath a canvas awning with senior commanders, pointing toward the western horizon while soldiers ready muskets and spears behind them.

dialogue.text: Marthanda Varma moved fast. He raised new levies, hardened his Nair corps, and anchored his defence on the seas he had once barely touched.

i18n.hi: मार्तांडा वर्मा ने भी रफ्तार पकड़ी। नई फौजें जुटाईं, नायर दस्तों को सख्त किया, और अपनी रक्षा उस समंदर पर टिकाई जिसे वो शायद ही छूते थे।

panels.shot: wide of Colachel bay with Dutch entrenchments and ships offshore
panels.action: The bay of Colachel curves under low hills, Dutch troops constructing earthworks and positioning cannon above the surf, their ships anchored just offshore in a grey, windswept sea.

dialogue.text: By mid‑1741 Dutch forces entrenched at Colachel, a small harbour town, linking their land camp to the guns of their ships.

i18n.hi: 1741 के बीच तक डच फौजें कोलाचेल नाम के छोटे बंदरगाह पर जमीं, जहां उनका कैम्प जहाज़ों की तोपों से जुड़ा था।

panels.shot: ground-level shot among Mukkuvar fishermen and Marakkar traders watching the build-up
panels.action: Mukkuvar fishermen, nets slung over shoulders, and Marakkar sea merchants in long coats stand on the sand, watching the Dutch positions and Travancore scouts with wary, calculating eyes as clouds pile over the sea.

dialogue.text: On these shores, Mukkuvar fishers and Marakkar traders read the tide of war. Their boats, harbours and news would weigh heavily on both sides.

i18n.hi: इन तटों पर मुक्कुवर मछुआरे और मरक्कार व्यापारी जंग की धार नाप रहे थे। उनकी नावें, घाट और खबरें दोनों तरफ तराजू झुकाती थीं।

panels.shot: low-angle of Travancore troops arriving over a rise toward Colachel
panels.action: Travancore infantry and Nair warriors crest a low ridge overlooking Colachel, monsoon rain streaking their faces, as Marthanda Varma rides behind them under an umbrella, gazing down at the Dutch camp.

dialogue.text: Travancore’s army marched hard through rain and heat, closing on Colachel before the Dutch could fully secure their line.

i18n.hi: त्रावणकोर की फौज बारिश और गर्मी चीरती तेज़ी से चली, और डच अपनी पूरी लकीर जमाते उससे पहले ही कोलाचेल पर आ धमकी।

panels.shot: split composition showing Dutch cannon line facing Travancore ranks
panels.action: On one side Dutch soldiers under De Lannoy stand by lined cannon and matchlocks behind earthworks; opposite them, Travancore ranks steady themselves, shields and muskets ready, with Marthanda Varma’s banner fluttering in the wet wind.

dialogue.text: On 10 August 1741 the monsoon sky hung low as Dutch firepower faced Travancore’s crowded ranks across the soaked sands of Colachel.

i18n.hi: 10 अगस्त 1741 को मानसून की नीची छतरी के नीचे डच तोपों के सामने त्रावणकोर कीぎठी हुई कतारें भीगी रेत पर खड़ी थीं।

panels.shot: close on De Lannoy giving orders amid the opening of battle
panels.action: Eustachius De Lannoy, rain‑slick helmet on, leans forward on the parapet shouting orders as his men ignite slow matches and swing their cannon toward advancing Travancore lines.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma_and_eustachius_de_lannoy
dialogue.text: Hold your line. Fire by volley, not by fear.

i18n.hi: पंक्ति मत तोड़ो। डर से नहीं, इशारे पर एक साथ गोली चलाओ।

panels.shot: dynamic wide of the battlefield under heavy rain, emphasizing movement but not gore
panels.action: Sheets of rain blur the clash as Dutch cannon belch smoke, Travancore musketeers fire back from advancing ranks, and war elephants loom in the background while the sandy ground turns to churned mud.

dialogue.text: The battle roared through rain and thunder. Smoke rolled over sand as volley answered volley, and neither side would yield.

i18n.hi: जंग बारिश और गरज में दहाड़ उठी। धुएं की चादर रेत पर लुढ़की, हर बोली के जवाब में बोली, और कोई पक्ष पीछे न हटा।

panels.shot: medium on Mukkuvar boats and local craft moving in the choppy bay
panels.action: Small coastal boats, rowed by local crews, dart between anchored Dutch ships and the shore as waves heave, some craft turning away, others hugging the surf line under watchful eyes.

dialogue.text: Tradition remembers daring night raids and decoy guns, but the record is plainer: logistics faltered, local currents shifted, and Dutch coordination with their fleet frayed.

i18n.hi: कहानियों में रात की धांसू घुसपैठें और नकली तोपें हैं, पर दस्तावेज़ साफ कहते हैं: रसद डगमगाई, स्थानीय हवा बदली, और बेड़े से डच तालमेल घिसट गया।

panels.shot: low wide shot of Travancore counter-attack overrunning abandoned Dutch guns
panels.action: Travancore soldiers surge over abandoned Dutch earthworks, seizing silent cannon as smoke drifts away, while in the distance Dutch troops fall back toward the shoreline and their ships.

dialogue.text: As the day wore on, Dutch positions buckled. With reinforcements delayed and the shore no safe refuge, their line broke under Travancore’s push.

i18n.hi: दिन चढ़ते‑चढ़ते डच मोर्चे थकने लगे। मदद अटकी रही, तट भी सुरक्षित न रहा, और त्रावणकोर के धक्के से उनकी लकीर टूट गई।

panels.shot: intimate medium of De Lannoy and a small group of officers surrounded by Travancore soldiers
panels.action: Eustachius De Lannoy and fellow officers stand disarmed on the damp sand, guarded by Travancore soldiers, their faces a mix of exhaustion and grim composure as captured Dutch flags droop nearby.

dialogue.text: Twenty‑four Dutch officers fell into Travancore hands. Among them stood Eustachius De Lannoy, a captain whose war had ended in a foreign camp.

i18n.hi: चौबीस डच अफसर त्रावणकोर के कब्जे में आए। इनमें यूस्टाखियुस डे लानॉय भी था, वो कप्तान जिसकी जंग अब परायी छावनी में खत्म हुई।

panels.shot: interior Travancore camp, low-angle on Marthanda Varma regarding the prisoners
panels.action: Inside a large tent lit by oil lamps, Marthanda Varma sits on a simple raised seat as De Lannoy and other captured officers stand before him, guarded yet unshackled, the sound of distant waves faintly audible.

dialogue.text: Here the story bent unexpectedly. The king who had broken the Dutch line did not rush to humiliate their officers.

i18n.hi: यहीं कथा अचानक मुड़ी। डच पंक्ति तोड़ने वाला राजा उनके अफसरों को बेइज़्जत करने को नहीं भागा।

panels.shot: close, respectful two-shot of Marthanda Varma and De Lannoy facing each other
panels.action: Marthanda Varma leans slightly forward, studying De Lannoy’s worn face; De Lannoy stands straight, meeting the king’s gaze with guarded respect, raindrops still on his armour.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma_and_eustachius_de_lannoy
dialogue.text: You know their drills, their guns. Serve Travancore, and live.

i18n.hi: तुम उनके अभ्यास, उनकी बंदूकें जानते हो। त्रावणकोर की सेवा करो, और ज़िंदा रहो।

panels.shot: medium close-up on De Lannoy’s conflicted expression as he considers
panels.action: De Lannoy’s face fills the frame, torn between defeat and opportunity, eyes flicking from the king to the soldiers, his hands loosely clasped before him.

dialogue.speaker: marthanda_varma_and_eustachius_de_lannoy
dialogue.text: Better to build than to sink with a crumbling Company.

i18n.hi: डूबती कंपनी के साथ डूबने से अच्छा, नई दीवारें खड़ी करना है।

panels.shot: training-ground wide showing De Lannoy drilling Travancore troops
panels.action: On a dry parade ground, De Lannoy, now in a mix of European coat and local garments, demonstrates musket drill to lines of Travancore soldiers, correcting a stance while officers watch closely.

dialogue.text: So the captured captain became Valiya Kappittan, the Great Captain, reshaping Travancore’s army along European lines.

i18n.hi: इसी तरह कैद कप्तान बन गया ‘वलिया कप्तान’ – बड़ा कप्तान – जिसने त्रावणकोर की फौज को यूरोपी ढांचे में ढाला।

panels.shot: wide shot of a new stone fort under construction on a hill
panels.action: Workers and soldiers labour on a massive stone fort atop a hill, bastions taking shape as De Lannoy and Marthanda Varma inspect plans together, the landscape of Travancore stretching beyond.

dialogue.text: Under his guidance, forts rose, artillery parks grew, and the kingdom learned to blend its old courage with new machines of war.

i18n.hi: उसकी रहनुमाई में किले उठे, तोपखाने बढ़े, और राज्य ने अपनी पुरानी बहादुरी को नई युद्ध मशीनों से मिला दिया।

panels.shot: medium inside a Dutch office, an official reading news of Colachel
panels.action: In a sombre Dutch office on the Malabar coast, a VOC official reads a letter with furrowed brow, a small painting of a ship behind him, while another officer stares out toward the sea.

dialogue.text: For the VOC, Colachel was a wound. Their records speak of lost officers, shattered prestige, and a new wariness toward inland kings.

i18n.hi: VOC के लिए कोलाचेल गहरा घाव था। उनके दस्तावेज़ गिरे अफसरों, टूटी प्रतिष्ठा और अंदरूनी राजाओं से नई हिचक की बात करते हैं।

panels.shot: documentary-like shot of a Dutch-Travancore treaty being signed later
panels.action: At a simple table, Dutch representatives and Travancore officials sign a treaty on parchment, hands steady, as witnesses stand behind them beneath a ceiling fan slowly turning.

dialogue.text: In time the letters turned to treaties. The Company that had come to dictate terms now bargained cautiously with the kingdom that had broken its line.

i18n.hi: समय के साथ खतों की जगह संधियों ने ली। जो कंपनी शर्तें सुनाने आई थी, वही अब उस राज्य से संभलकर सौदे कर रही थी जिसने उसकी लकीर तोड़ी थी।

panels.shot: sunset wide of Marthanda Varma and De Lannoy overlooking the sea from a fort bastion
panels.action: At sunset, Marthanda Varma and the older De Lannoy stand on a fort bastion, looking out over the calm sea and the pepper‑green hills behind them, flags of Travancore stirring in the evening breeze.

dialogue.text: Colachel did not end with a victory cry; it echoed in drills, in fort walls, and in a foreign captain who turned from invader to architect.

i18n.hi: कोलाचेल का अंत सिर्फ विजय के नारे से नहीं हुआ; वो अभ्यास मैदानों, किलों की दीवारों और उस पराये कप्तान में गूंजा जिसने हमलावर से शिल्पी का रूप लिया।

panels.shot: reflective close on the waves washing the Colachel shore, footprints fading
panels.action: Gentle waves wash over the Colachel shore, softening footprints and cart tracks in the wet sand as fishing boats rest pulled up under the starlit sky.

dialogue.text: On this small monsoon shore, a pepper war showed how a battlefield can break an empire’s pride and turn an enemy into a teacher.

i18n.hi: यहीं छोटे से मानसूनी तट पर, मिर्च की जंग ने दिखाया कि कैसे एक मैदान साम्राज्य की शान तोड़ सकता है और दुश्मन को गुरु बना सकता है।

title_i18n.hi: कोलाचेल 1741 – भारत ने VOC को हराया

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Monsoon Shore, a Pepper War Topples an Empire’s Pride
subtitle_i18n.hi: मानसूनी किनारे पर, काली मिर्च की जंग में ढही साम्राज्य की शान
